toc.topic: Course Orientation, Ethics, Laws and Responsible Disclosure
subtopics: Course objectives, outcomes and assessment overview
Roles and responsibilities of ethical hackers / penetration testers
Codes of conduct, professional ethics and industry standards (e.g., CEH, OSCP, ISO 27001 implications)
Legal frameworks, authorization, contracts and scope definition (domestic and international considerations)
Rules of engagement, safe testing practices, and handling sensitive data
Responsible disclosure process and coordination with incident response
Risk management and decision-making during tests

toc.topic: Methodology, Lab Setup and Tools Overview
subtopics: Penetration testing methodologies (PTES, OSSTMM, NIST 800-115) and test planning
Setting up safe lab environments: virtual lab, staging networks, and containment
Essential tool categories and workflow (recon, scanning, exploitation, post-exploit, reporting)
Overview of commonly used tools: Nmap, Wireshark, Burp Suite, Metasploit, Nikto, OpenVAS, sqlmap, etc.
Managing artifacts: data collection, logs, evidence preservation and tool configuration
Lab setup hands-on: building a reproducible VM lab and installing/configuring key tools
Active vs passive reconnaissance: concepts and tradeoffs
DNS interrogation, WHOIS, zone transfers, and subdomain discovery
Using search engines, social media, code repositories, and metadata for OSINT
Gathering infrastructure intelligence: IP ranges, cloud assets, CDN and service discovery
Footprinting web applications, identifying technologies and third-party services
Automated OSINT tools and frameworks (theHarvester, Recon-ng, Shodan, Censys)
Hands-on lab: OSINT exercise — map a target's external footprint and create an asset inventory (guided)
Network scanning fundamentals: TCP/UDP scanning, timing, and evasion techniques
Nmap advanced usage: scripting (NSE), version detection, OS fingerprinting and output parsing
Port scanning strategies, interpretation of results and prioritization
Service enumeration: SMB, LDAP, SNMP, SSH, FTP, databases and web services
Banner grabbing, protocol analysis and fingerprinting
Vulnerability scanners overview (Nessus/OpenVAS) and how to validate findings
Hands-on lab: perform targeted scanning and enumeration on lab hosts; interpret and triage results
Vulnerability assessment vs exploitation: scope and objectives
Classifying vulnerabilities: CVE, CVSS scoring, exploitability and business impact
Correlating scanner output with manual verification to reduce false positives
Public exploit research and safe use of exploit databases (Exploit-DB, Metasploit modules)
Prioritization frameworks and remediation guidance
Hands-on lab: analyze scanned findings, validate key vulnerabilities and produce a risk-ranked checklist
Exploitation concepts: payloads, shells, exploits, and exploit reliability
Using Metasploit Framework: modules, listeners, payloads, and post modules
Buffer overflows and memory corruption basics (conceptual overview and safe demonstration)
Safe exploitation practices and avoiding collateral damage
Authentication bypass techniques, default credentials and weak crypto
Hands-on lab: controlled exploitation with Metasploit on lab targets; capturing shells and documenting steps
Web application architecture, request lifecycle and common components
Injection attacks (SQLi, Command Injection) — detection and exploitation
Authentication and session management weaknesses
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), CSRF and other client-side attacks
Insecure deserialization, broken access control and server-side vulnerabilities
Using Burp Suite effectively: intercepting proxy, repeater, intruder, scanner basics
Automated vs manual testing techniques and fuzzing approaches
Hands-on lab: OWASP Top 10 practical exercise using vulnerable web apps (e.g., DVWA, Juice Shop) with Burp Suite and sqlmap

toc.topic: Network Attacks, Pivoting and Lateral Movement
subtopics: Network-level attacks: ARP spoofing, MITM, DNS poisoning and spoofing basics
Capturing and analyzing network traffic with Wireshark and tcpdump
Exploitation of network services and relay techniques (e.g., SMB relay)
Establishing footholds, pivoting techniques and use of proxychains/SSH tunnels
Use of covert channels and tunneling (DNS, HTTP(S)) and detection implications
Hands-on lab: perform a simulated lateral movement exercise and pivot from a compromised host to internal targets
Wireless fundamentals: 802.11 overview, encryption types (WEP/WPA/WPA2/WPA3) and attack surface
Assessing wireless networks: discovery, rogue APs, deauth attacks and WPA handshake capture
Bluetooth and IoT/mobile considerations and common misuse patterns
Tools for wireless testing: Aircrack-ng suite, Kismet and mobile-focused tools
Hands-on lab: capture and analyze wireless traffic in a controlled environment; attempt WPA2 handshake capture and demonstrate deauth (lab-safe)

toc.topic: Post-Exploitation, Privilege Escalation and Data Exfiltration
subtopics: Post-exploitation objectives: persistence, credential harvesting, lateral movement and data staging
Windows and Linux privilege escalation techniques and identification of privilege escalation vectors
Credential dumping basics (LSASS, /etc/passwd shadow) and safe handling
Maintaining access: backdoors, scheduled tasks, services and startup items (ethical considerations)
Data exfiltration methods and minimizing detection
Hands-on lab: perform post-exploitation tasks in lab, practice privilege escalation techniques and document findings
Structuring professional penetration testing reports: executive summary, technical findings, risk ratings and remediation steps
Creating reproducible test evidence: logs, screenshots, PoCs and safe artifact handling
Delivering technical and non-technical briefings to stakeholders
Remediation validation and retest recommendations
Introduction to red/blue team collaboration and basic defensive controls to mitigate common attack patterns
Hands-on: produce a sample finding report from lab exercise and present remediation recommendations

toc.topic: Capstone Practical: Full-scope Penetration Test and Course Wrap-up
subtopics: Live capstone exercise: plan and execute a limited-scope penetration test in the lab (recon, scan, exploit, post-exploit, report)
Team coordination, time management and attack documentation during the exercise
Assessment: practical deliverables review and instructor feedback
Consolidated best practices checklist and career next steps (certifications, continuous learning)
Course debrief, Q&A, resources and recommended reading
